name: Nepliget 1936
notes: Népliget, the People's Park in the Kőbánya district of Budapest, whose ordinary park roads were closed to make a 4.988 km street circuit for the first Hungarian Grand Prix on 21 June 1936. Twenty-two turns and only one straight - the 750 m central axis carrying the start line - so the lap was very nearly a continuous series of corners, run anti-clockwise. Bernd Rosemeyer put the Auto Union on pole at 2:38.15, but Tazio Nuvolari won for Alfa Romeo over 50 laps and 250 km and took the fastest lap at 2:35.68, beating the German teams on a circuit that suited neither. Fourteen cars started. Hungary did not hold another Grand Prix until 1986.
author: carTOON (barcika)
